title: Beatrix and the Vow
premise: August Blackwood, a wedding planner who swore off her own happy endings after her mother's death and a broken engagement, inherits a crumbling orchard deed that inexplicably lists two names: hers and Theo Marsh, the baker who left her ten years ago without a goodbye. Forced to untangle the legal tangle left by her late grandmother—who secretly bought the orchard to trap them both into finishing what they started—August must work the land alongside Theo while planning one last wedding that could save both the orchard and her business. As the bakery lease deadline and a rival developer close in, August finally says the rehearsed sentence she has carried for a decade—'I stayed because I loved you'—and chooses to stay visible, in love, and rooted. The book ends with the orchard saved, the deed rewritten in both their names by choice rather than inheritance, and a small, unpolished wedding among the pear trees.
about_author: Ada Nakamura is a former estate lawyer who traded contract law for love stories after inheriting her family's century-old pear orchard. She writes from a converted packing shed, where she bakes badly and plots happily.

chapters.title: The Past Tense of Love
chapters.summary: August's POV. She flawlessly executes a stranger's wedding while refusing the officiant's question about her own love life, revealing she keeps every feeling in past tense. Beat: establish her armor—professional intimacy without personal risk—and the bakery lease notice that opens the wound.

chapters.title: Two Names on a Deed
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her grandmother's lawyer delivers the orchard deed, and August discovers Theo Marsh's name beside hers, co-owned and unbreakable. Beat: shock and fury; the inheritance she wanted has arrived with a ghost attached.

chapters.title: The Man at the Gate
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives at the orchard expecting an empty property and finds August, ten years older and colder. Their first exchange is all legal language hiding old hurt. Beat: recognition, resentment, and the first crack in his own silence.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: August's POV. They draft a hostile co-ownership agreement: split the harvest, sell fast, never speak of the past. Beat: darkly funny negotiation scenes where every clause is a scar; August convinces herself proximity is survivable.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo walks the orchard alone and finds his grandmother's handwriting on old grafting tags—she and August's grandmother were best friends who engineered this match. Beat: guilt surfaces; he begins to understand the goodbye he never gave.

chapters.title: The Wedding She Won't Plan
chapters.summary: August's POV. A desperate bride begs August to take an impossible orchard wedding—her only option to save her company's finances. Beat: August must work on the very land she's trying to escape, and Theo's bread becomes an accidental peace offering.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Working the trees together, Theo teaches August her grandmother's grafting techniques; hands touch, laughter escapes. Beat: reluctant warmth; August catches herself remembering instead of forgetting.

chapters.title: The Sentence in the Drawer
chapters.summary: August's POV. August finds her grandmother's letter revealing she knew about the broken engagement—and about the sentence August has rehearsed for a decade. Beat: the letter demands she say it aloud before the lease ends; August burns it instead.

chapters.title: Rain on the Packing Shed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A storm traps them in the packing shed; Theo nearly tells the truth about why he left—his father's bankruptcy, the debt, the shame—but stops at the edge. Beat: almost-confession, charged near-kiss, retreat.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: August's POV. A developer offers a fortune for the orchard, and the wedding client's venue falls through, threatening both the orchard and August's business. Beat: stakes double; selling starts looking like mercy instead of betrayal.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, flashback chapter. The night Theo left: his father's collapse, the forged signature on the bakery loan, and the choice to disappear rather than drag August into ruin. Beat: reframe the villain as a coward protecting her; reader's heart shifts.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: August's POV. The town's harvest festival forces August and Theo to host together; old neighbors reveal how much the grandmothers plotted, and how much the town rooted for them. Beat: belonging tugs at August's invisibility; a dance under string lights.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: August's POV. August finds a photo of the two grandmothers signing the deed together, dated the week after Theo left—proof this was a rescue mission, not a matchmaking whim. Beat: grief for the grandmothers softens into gratitude; she almost tells Theo.

chapters.title: Misread Vows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo sees August with her ex-fiancé at a venue tasting and misreads the meeting as reconciliation. Beat: jealousy he has no right to; he signs preliminary papers with the developer in self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: August's POV. The bakery lease expires and the developer's offer deadline lands the same week; the wedding client threatens to walk. Beat: everything August built on control collapses at once; she realizes the sentence can't wait for perfect conditions.

chapters.title: What Theo Buried
chapters.summary: August's POV. August finds Theo's father's loan documents in the shed and finally understands why he vanished. Beat: anger transmutes into aching comprehension; she goes to find him before he sells everything again.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the rain-soaked orchard, August says the rehearsed sentence—'I stayed because I loved you'—and Theo finally gives his confession in full. Beat: climax of the emotional arc; the decade of silence breaks open, raw and unresolved.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Almost Wasn't
chapters.summary: August's POV. The orchard wedding arrives amid the sale crisis; August plans it as her last act of professional love, and Theo fights the developer with the grandmothers' original deed clause. Beat: external climax; the town rallies, the client's vows echo their own.

chapters.title: Signatures
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The developer is beaten by the deed's heritage clause; Theo and August rewrite the co-ownership agreement—this time with honest terms and both signatures freely given. Beat: the legal instrument becomes a love letter; quiet triumph.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: August's POV. The first quiet days of the new arrangement: slow mornings, the bakery reopened in the orchard's packing shed, grief for her mother finally spoken aloud. Beat: tenderness after the storm; belonging stops being terrifying.

chapters.title: An Unpolished Wedding
chapters.summary: August's POV, with Theo. They marry under the pear trees—no planner, no perfect timeline, the town as witnesses. Beat: the woman who didn't believe in weddings chooses one; the vow mirrors the sentence she finally said.

chapters.title: In Present Tense
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue-style. One year later: the orchard thriving, a new couple's wedding booked, August writing vows in present tense for the first time. Beat: full resolution—memory honored, inheritance claimed, belonging chosen.
